short: Boltzmann: two solutions from one gas

title.title: Hard-sphere Boltzmann: two solutions from one initial gas
title.subtitle: Claim: one initial density on the torus has two distinct global solutions, both with entropy dissipation

plain: Start a gas in one exact state, and the equations allow two different futures

object.heading: Schematic: one initial density $f_0$, two global solutions

beats.text: DiPerna–Lions (1989) solutions exist globally. Are they determined by their data?
Claim: no. Cold jets on a hot background, at ever smaller scales, split one gas in two
Lean covers the renormalized version; exact local conservation is paper only

steps: Build a gas of cold jets on a hot background, at shrinking scales
In one future a rare collision triggers a branching cascade
In the other it does not: two solutions from one start

achievement.label: Uniqueness of DiPerna–Lions solutions (1989)
statement: f_0 \;\longmapsto\; f_1 \ne f_2, \ \ \text{both global, both dissipate entropy}
achievement.context: Gismondi, Golding and Novack conjectured nonuniqueness this August; hard spheres on the torus
achievement.note: The data are deliberately singular; uniqueness in tamer classes stands

verify.detail: Lean: the renormalized version. The 78-page exact-conservation paper is not formalized
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with both papers; we did not build it

voice.text: Boltzmann solutions exist forever. Are they fixed by their start? Cold jets say no.
A rare collision cascade happens in one future and not the other.
Claimed: two distinct global solutions, one start.

sources.quote: DiPerna and Lions built global solutions of the Boltzmann equation in 1989.

sources.ref: article, Boltzmann's equation: two solutions from one initial gas
sources.quote: Gismondi, Golding and Novack conjectured this August that they are not. Family 363 confirms it for hard spheres on the torus.

sources.ref: article, Boltzmann's equation: two solutions from one initial gas
sources.quote: One carefully built initial density, cold jets on a hot background concentrated at ever smaller scales, admits two distinct global solutions that keep entropy dissipation.

sources.ref: article, Boltzmann's equation: two solutions from one initial gas
sources.quote: That comes from a 78-page paper dated 5 October that is not formalized. Lean covers the earlier, weaker renormalized-solution version
Data are deliberately singular (unbounded amplitudes at shrinking spatial scales, irrational axis, annular jets), so it does not contradict uniqueness results in bounded/near-Maxwellian classes.
